Mr. Rahim, the learned Advocate further submits that in view of the non obstante clause in Section 3 of the Ordinance, the provisions of the Ordinance shall override all other provisions including Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, as such, he submits, the defendant pre-emptor inspite of the order of pre-emption in his favour, is debarred from taking possession of the pre-empted land which is the homestead of the petitioners in a rural area. 

 8. It appears that one Salimuddin Mondal, the predecessor of the petitioners, purchased the suit property on 27.83.1995 and allegedly constructed his house thereon but the defendant-opposite party filed a pre-emption case under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy. Act being the Miscellaneous case no. 97 of 1984 against the said Slimuddin Mondal. He died during the pendency of the said case, as such, his heris, the present petitioners, contested the case but the defendant opposite party got pre-emption of the suit land by the judgment and order dated 14.01.1990 

 13. Again, in the case of Mokarram Hossain V. ADC (Rev.) Pabna 51 DLR(1999) 470, the eviction of the plaintiffs who had no title to the suit land was refused in view of the said provision. Section 6 of the Ordinance reads as follows: "6 No eviction, etc. from homestead. Any land used as a homestead by its owner in the rural area shall be exempted from all legal processes, including seizure, distress attachment or sale by any office, court or any other authority and the owner of such land shall not be divested or dispossessed of the land or evicted therefrom by any means. Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to the acquisition of such homestead under any law." The provision envisages that the homestead of an owner in a rural area is exempted from all legal processes. But in order to get such protection under the ordinance, the homestead must be in a rural area and the exemption from the legal processes is available only to an owner' of such a homestead. 

 16. The preamble of a statute is an important guide to understand and appreciate the intent and purport of any law. The preamble of the Ordinance reads as follows: An Ordinance to reform the law relating to land tenure, land holding and land transfer with a view to maximizing production and ensuring a better relationship between land owners and bargadars. Whereas it is expedient to reform the law relating to land tenure land holding and land transfer with a view to maximizing production and ensuring a better relationship between land owners and bargadars." Besides, the word 'owner' is defined in Section 2 of the Ordinance but again only in relation to a bargadar. It states as follows: (g) "owner" in relation to barga land, means the person from whom the hargadar gets the land for cultivation under a borga contract." So it is apparent that one has to read, understand and appreciate the scope of the word 'owner' as appearing in Section 6 of the Ordnance within the ambit of the said very Ordinance itself in its restrictive sense and not beyond it.
